paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.

model_annotations.German: The plot titled “GPT2-XL” illustrates how two metrics, Efficacy\_top and noise\_E, vary as the number of edits increases for two methods (AlphaEdit and MEMIT). The x-axis shows the number of edits on a linear scale, with labeled ticks at 500-unit intervals from 500 to 3000 and plotted points spanning approximately 300 to 3000 edits. The left y-axis is labeled “Efficacy\_top” on a linear scale, with labeled ticks from 30 to 100 at 10-unit intervals, while the right y-axis is labeled “noise\_E” on a linear scale, with labeled ticks from 0 to 140 at 20-unit intervals. AlphaEdit Efficacy\_top is shown as a red dashed line with square markers, starting near 99 at the first point (≈300 edits) and remaining near 99 through ≈1000 edits before declining to about 97 (≈1500), 95 (≈2000), 92 (≈2500), and about 86 at 3000. MEMIT Efficacy\_top is shown as a light-blue dashed line with square markers, beginning around 87 at ≈300–500 edits, then decreasing to about 79 at 1000, 76 at 1500, 60 at 2000, 36 at 2500, and about 26 at 3000. AlphaEdit noise\_E is shown as a red solid line with circular markers, rising gradually from roughly 6 at ≈300 edits to about 8 (500), 10 (1000), 12 (1500), 14 (2000), 15 (2500), and about 17 at 3000. MEMIT noise\_E is shown as a light-blue solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 10 at ≈300 edits to around 18 (500), 35 (1000), 50 (1500), 70 (2000), 105 (2500), and approximately 150 at 3000.
